ai_insights.executive_summary: CONDITIONAL GO: Average response time improved 25% (398ms to 299ms) and SLA pass rate rose 8.3pp year-over-year. However, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal p95 tail latency regressed from 1339ms to 2163ms, crossing the 1500ms SLA threshold and representing the primary bottleneck driver. Overall error rate remained flat at ~11%, confirming the release is viable with targeted tail latency mitigation.
highlights: Average response time across all percentiles dropped 25% (p99: 1454ms to 1148ms), driven by reduced processing overhead in the current test execution.
SLA pass rate improved from 29.2% to 37.5%, primarily due to latency compression in transactions with tight SLA targets (e.g., TC01_T_03, TC02_T_06, TC01_T_06 now passing where baseline breached).
TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal p95 tail latency spiked from 1339ms to 2163ms, crossing the 1500ms SLA threshold and representing the most significant regression in this release.
Error rate held steady at ~11% across both runs, indicating the latency improvements did not introduce new reliability risks but also did not resolve the underlying error source.
recommendations: [Database / Indexing]: Optimize search portal query paths and add targeted indexes to suppress p95 tail latency below 1500ms SLA threshold.

[Application Gateway / Thread Pool]: Audit and rebalance thread pool sizing and connection pool saturation points responsible for the persistent ~11% error rate across authentication and checkout transactions.

findings.title: TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal p95 Tail Latency Regression Past SLA Threshold
findings.observation: TC03_T_01 p95 latency increased from 1339ms to 2163ms, crossing the 1500ms SLA target despite overall average latency improvement of 25% across all transactions.
findings.why_it_matters: This tail latency spike risks user-facing delays for search interactions and could trigger SLA penalties for search-dominant user journeys during peak concurrency.
findings.recommendation: Profile the search portal's database query patterns and implement indexing, result pagination, or connection pooling optimizations to suppress p95 latency below 1500ms.

findings.title: SLA Pass Rate Improvement Driven by Latency Compression in Tight-SLA Transactions
findings.observation: Latency compression across 15 transactions shifted their p90/p95 below respective SLA targets, lifting the aggregate SLA pass rate from 29.2% to 37.5% despite unchanged error rate of ~11%.
findings.why_it_matters: The improvement demonstrates that recent architectural changes or test configuration adjustments successfully reduced median latency, expanding the user experience envelope for the majority of requests.
findings.recommendation: Maintain the latency-optimizing configuration changes and validate with a sustained-load test to confirm the SLA pass rate improvement is reproducible and stable.

findings.title: Error Rate Remains Flat at ~11% Across Both Runs
findings.observation: Both baseline and current runs report a stable 11% error rate, with 15+ transactions sustaining 100% error_rate_pct, suggesting a systemic error definition or underlying infrastructure issue unaffected by latency improvements.
findings.why_it_matters: The persistent error rate could mask performance gains and risks user trust; resolving the error source is critical for full SLA compliance.
findings.recommendation: Diagnose the root cause of the 100% error_rate_pct transactions (e.g., authentication token validation, session handling) and implement targeted fixes to reduce the error rate below the SLA threshold of 1.0%.
